analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: AI demand remains robust despite market jitters
key_insights: Tech led US equity declines on Thursday after reports of a lower-than-expected OpenAI revenue run rate raised concerns about AI demand growth. The Nasdaq fell 1.25%, its largest one-day drop since August.
UBS says the gap between earlier expectations and the reported OpenAI figures may partly reflect differences in revenue-recognition methods. Recent industry data still point to robust AI demand.

Meta's Muse AI assistant has over 6.6 million downloads and 1.8 million daily active users since launching a month ago (Sensor Tower). UBS reads this as early evidence of rising consumer AI agent adoption.

Semiconductor data points to sustained compute demand: TSMC reported a 51% rise in quarterly revenue, Samsung flagged an almost nine-fold jump in quarterly operating profit, Hon Hai beat quarterly sales estimates, and Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast.
UBS expects fundamentals to drive the AI trade in the coming weeks, with third-quarter earnings likely to show further demand for AI compute and infrastructure.

UBS expects average hyperscaler cloud revenue growth of 58% y/y for the September quarter, up from 48% in the June quarter. Consumer AI agents could add monetization through subscriptions, advertising and transactions.

UBS recommends a diversified tech approach: high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries of AI spending, megacap platforms and defensive tech firms. Investors should be more selective and disciplined given concerns over growth, financing and safety.

UBS sees the euro sell-off as overdone. EURUSD is up 0.2% to 1.1230 on Friday but has fallen nearly 4% in seven weeks. Positioning and options indicators show the dollar overbought and the euro oversold.
UBS sees an attractive opportunity to re-enter long EURUSD and expects a recovery toward 1.16 over the coming months. It would avoid chasing the dollar higher.

Fed Governor Waller said further hikes are likely needed but the Fed has 'some flexibility' on timing and hikes 'do not need to come at consecutive meetings'. Markets now price the next hike for December rather than October.
UBS's base case is a Fed hike in December while staying patient on data. It believes equities can cope with moderately higher rates alongside resilient growth and strong earnings.

sector_views.rationale: Favors high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries of AI spending, megacap platforms and defensive tech firms, with more selectivity given volatility risks.

earnings_insights: UBS expects average hyperscaler cloud revenue growth of 58% y/y for the September quarter (UBS estimate), versus 48% reported for the June quarter.

TSMC reported a 51% rise in quarterly revenue this week. Samsung flagged an almost nine-fold jump in quarterly operating profit ahead of full earnings (preliminary, not the full report). Hon Hai beat its quarterly sales estimates. Marvell raised its fiscal 2028 revenue forecast.
US third-quarter earnings season starts in the coming week.

UBS expects periods of volatility in the AI trade from concerns over growth, financing and safety.
